questions.enonce_markdown:
Create the above tables using your RDBMS. Write the corresponding SQL code used for each table in the spaces provided below. *[6 marks]*

(i) Player

(ii) Club

(iii) Coach
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each table needs a `CREATE TABLE` statement that gives every field its name, a data type of the right kind and size, and declares the primary key (marked with an asterisk). Mapping used: Text of size n becomes `VARCHAR(n)`, "Short integer" becomes `SMALLINT`, "Long integer" becomes `INTEGER` and Date becomes `DATE` (the *Day/Month/Year* format is a display format chosen in the RDBMS, not part of the type).

**(i) Player** *(2 marks)*

```sql
CREATE TABLE Player (
    PlayerID    VARCHAR(6)  PRIMARY KEY,
    ClubID      VARCHAR(10),
    Name        VARCHAR(30),
    Position    SMALLINT,
    MatchPlayed INTEGER,
    Goals       INTEGER
);
```

**(ii) Club** *(2 marks)*

```sql
CREATE TABLE Club (
    ClubID       VARCHAR(10) PRIMARY KEY,
    CoachID      VARCHAR(10),
    Country      VARCHAR(30),
    NoTitles     SMALLINT,
    YearCreation DATE
);
```

**(iii) Coach** *(2 marks)*

```sql
CREATE TABLE Coach (
    CoachID     VARCHAR(10) PRIMARY KEY,
    ClubID      VARCHAR(10),
    Name        VARCHAR(30),
    Titles      SMALLINT,
    Nationality VARCHAR(20),
    Age         SMALLINT
);
```

*Remarks.* (1) `PlayerID`, `ClubID` and `CoachID` are text keys because their examples (`21A001`, `BARCA001`, `CHEL001`) mix letters and digits. (2) `Player.ClubID` refers to `Club`, and `Club.CoachID` and `Coach.ClubID` refer to each other. Because of this circular dependency the foreign keys are added once the data are loaded, for example `ALTER TABLE Player ADD CONSTRAINT fk_player_club FOREIGN KEY (ClubID) REFERENCES Club (ClubID);` (syntax of MySQL, PostgreSQL and Oracle; SQLite has no `ADD CONSTRAINT`). The three statements above were run successfully with SQLite; in MS Access use `TEXT(10)`, `SHORT` and `LONG` for the same fields.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw an entity-relationship diagram involving the three tables stated above. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
An entity-relationship diagram shows each table as an entity (with its attributes and primary key) and joins the entities by relationships with their cardinalities. The foreign keys give the relationships:

- `Player.ClubID` refers to `Club.ClubID`: a club has many players, a player belongs to one club, so **Club 1 - N Player**;
- `Club.CoachID` and `Coach.ClubID` refer to each other: a club has one coach and a coach manages one club, so **Coach 1 - 1 Club**.

```
+--------------------+ 1       1 +--------------------+
| COACH              |-----------| CLUB               |
| CoachID (PK)       |  manages  | ClubID (PK)        |
| ClubID (FK)        |           | CoachID (FK)       |
| Name               |           | Country            |
| Titles             |           | NoTitles           |
| Nationality        |           | YearCreation       |
| Age                |           +--------------------+
+--------------------+                     | 1
                                           | has
                                           | N
                                 +--------------------+
                                 | PLAYER             |
                                 | PlayerID (PK)      |
                                 | ClubID (FK)        |
                                 | Name               |
                                 | Position           |
                                 | MatchPlayed        |
                                 | Goals              |
                                 +--------------------+
```

Marking: three entities correctly labelled with their keys (1 mark), relationship Club-Player with the cardinality 1 to many (1 mark), relationship Coach-Club with the cardinality 1 to 1 (1 mark).

questions.enonce_markdown: In your RDBMS, create an SQL query that displays the names of players, and of their coaches, who scored above 100 goals and played less than 80 matches. Also write below the query statements used. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The names of the players are in `Player`, those of the coaches are in `Coach`, so the two tables are joined. A player and the coach of the same club share the `ClubID` value, hence the join condition `Player.ClubID = Coach.ClubID`. Both tables have a `Name` field, so each name is qualified by its table and given an alias. The two conditions of the question are combined with `AND`: **above 100** is the strict inequality `Goals > 100` and **less than 80** is the strict inequality `MatchPlayed < 80`.

```sql
SELECT Player.Name AS PlayerName, Coach.Name AS CoachName
FROM Player
INNER JOIN Coach ON Player.ClubID = Coach.ClubID
WHERE Player.Goals > 100
  AND Player.MatchPlayed < 80;
```

*Marking:* `SELECT` of the two names (1), `FROM` with the join of Player and Coach (2), `Goals > 100` (1), `MatchPlayed < 80` combined by `AND` (1).

With the data of question 3 the query returns three rows. The player `Paolo Neri` (exactly 100 goals) is excluded by the strict inequality, and `Samuel Okoro` (110 goals but 95 matches) by the condition on matches:

| PlayerName | CoachName |
|---|---|
| Diego Alvarez | Marco Silva |
| Tom Baker | Pierre Dubois |
| Ahmed Said | Carlos Ruiz |

An equivalent query goes through the `Club` table (also run and giving the same three rows):

```sql
SELECT Player.Name AS PlayerName, Coach.Name AS CoachName
FROM Player, Club, Coach
WHERE Player.ClubID = Club.ClubID
  AND Club.CoachID = Coach.CoachID
  AND Player.Goals > 100
  AND Player.MatchPlayed < 80;
```

questions.enonce_markdown: Save the query as the file namesofplayers and print a copy of the table it produced. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a graphical RDBMS (for example MS Access) the query is saved under the name `namesofplayers` (File - Save As). In a SQL environment the same effect is a stored query, that is a view:

```sql
CREATE VIEW namesofplayers AS
SELECT Player.Name AS PlayerName, Coach.Name AS CoachName
FROM Player
INNER JOIN Coach ON Player.ClubID = Coach.ClubID
WHERE Player.Goals > 100
  AND Player.MatchPlayed < 80;
```

Running `SELECT * FROM namesofplayers;` displays the result table, which is then printed (1 mark for saving under the exact name, 1 mark for the printed result):

| PlayerName | CoachName |
|---|---|
| Diego Alvarez | Marco Silva |
| Tom Baker | Pierre Dubois |
| Ahmed Said | Carlos Ruiz |
